notice: Human-approved rules. Each rule references a catalog entry (catalog.json) and lists checks; every check declares its data source. Only checks with an automated detector AND an available data source (AVAILABLE_DATA_SOURCES) are executed; the others are reported as not executed. Approved rules always take precedence over LLM candidates for the same entry.

rules.source_quote: Since this release, the hostname does not accept such type of wildcard and those patterns will be managed as if the wildcard is after the hostname https://example.com/*.
rules.remediation: Replace every valid redirect URI with a wildcard right after the host (e.g. https://example.com*) with an explicit host followed by a path (e.g. https://example.com/*), register other hosts explicitly, and prefer exact redirect URIs.

checks.what_to_check: Valid redirect URIs of every client
checks.how_to_check: Look for redirect URIs with a '*' right after or inside the host name, e.g. https://example.com*; the full wildcard https://* is still accepted
checks.impact_signal: The client relies on the wildcard matching other host names, which is no longer the case
checks.evidence_quote: Previously patterns like https://example.com* were accepted and lead to allow unintended domains like https://example.com.other.domain.com.

checks.what_to_check: Authorization requests whose redirect_uri host differs from the registered host but matched the hostname wildcard
checks.how_to_check: For clients flagged on the realm export, compare the redirect_uri query parameter of /protocol/openid-connect/auth requests with the registered host
checks.impact_signal: Requests to hosts like example.com.other.domain.com that will be rejected after the upgrade
checks.evidence_quote: Since this release, the hostname does not accept such type of wildcard and those patterns will be managed as if the wildcard is after the hostname https://example.com/*.

rules.source_quote: This functionality was deprecated in Keycloak 18 and has been removed in this version in favor of following the OpenID Connect specification.
rules.remediation: Implement OpenID Connect RP-Initiated Logout: send post_logout_redirect_uri together with id_token_hint (or client_id) and register the URI in 'Valid post logout redirect URIs'.

checks.what_to_check: Calls to the OIDC logout endpoint with the legacy redirect_uri parameter
checks.how_to_check: Filter access log records on /protocol/openid-connect/logout with a redirect_uri query parameter
checks.impact_signal: Any such request: it fails after the upgrade
checks.evidence_quote: Previous versions of Keycloak had supported automatic logout of the user and redirecting to the application by opening logout endpoint URL such as http(s)://example-host/auth/realms/my-realm-name/protocol/openid-connect/logout?redirect_uri=encodedRedirectUri.

checks.how_to_check: Search startup options, keycloak.conf and environment variables for --spi-login-protocol-openid-connect-legacy-logout-redirect-uri and --spi-login-protocol-openid-connect-suppress-logout-confirmation-screen
checks.impact_signal: Option set: the server relied on the removed behaviour (and the option is no longer recognised)
checks.evidence_quote: As part of this change the following related configuration options for the SPI have been removed:

rules.source_quote: As this has led to a hard-to-configure URL filtering, for example, in reverse proxies, the normalization is now disabled, and Keycloak responds with an HTTP 400 response code.
rules.remediation: Normalize request URLs in client libraries and reverse proxies (collapse '//' and resolve dot segments). The option http-accept-non-normalized-paths=true restores the old behaviour only temporarily: it is deprecated.

checks.what_to_check: HTTP requests whose path contains '//' or dot segments
checks.how_to_check: Filter access log paths matching '//' or '/./' or '/../'
checks.impact_signal: Such requests get HTTP 400 after the upgrade
checks.evidence_quote: As this has led to a hard-to-configure URL filtering, for example, in reverse proxies, the normalization is now disabled, and Keycloak responds with an HTTP 400 response code.

checks.how_to_check: Check startup options / keycloak.conf / environment for http-accept-non-normalized-paths=true
checks.impact_signal: Option enabled: the old behaviour is kept for now, but the option is deprecated
checks.evidence_quote: To revert to the previous behavior and to accept non-normalized URLs, set the option http-accept-non-normalized-paths to true.

checks.how_to_check: After the upgrade, enable debug logging for org.keycloak.quarkus.runtime.services.RejectNonNormalizedPathFilter and look for its messages
checks.impact_signal: Messages from the filter identify rejected requests
checks.evidence_quote: To analyze rejected requests in the server log, enable debug logging for org.keycloak.quarkus.runtime.services.RejectNonNormalizedPathFilter.

rules.source_quote: In this release, the role and client mappers now map to a single value from the effective roles of a user when they are marked as single-valued (Multivalued disabled).
rules.remediation: If consumers expect all roles, enable 'Multivalued' on the role mapper and read the claim as a JSON array; otherwise update consumers that parsed the former stringified JSON array, which now receive a single role value.

checks.what_to_check: Realm/client role protocol mappers with Multivalued disabled
checks.how_to_check: Inspect protocol mappers of type oidc-usermodel-realm-role-mapper / oidc-usermodel-client-role-mapper with multivalued=false
checks.impact_signal: The claim changes from a stringified JSON array to a single role value
checks.evidence_quote: In this release, the role and client mappers now map to a single value from the effective roles of a user when they are marked as single-valued (Multivalued disabled).

checks.what_to_check: Applications parsing the role claim of single-valued mappers
checks.how_to_check: Review the token parsing code of the flagged clients
checks.impact_signal: Code that expects a JSON array encoded as a string
checks.evidence_quote: Before this release, both realm (User Realm Role) and client (User Client Role) protocol mappers were mapping a stringfied JSON array when the Multivalued setting was disabled.

controls.title: Calls on monitored endpoints not attributable to a client
controls.remediation: Enable MDC (log-mdc-enabled with the clientId key) and make clients send client_id explicitly, so that runtime evidence can be attributed to a Keycloak client.

checks.what_to_check: Calls on /realms/* without a client id
checks.how_to_check: Access log records with client_id = anonymous
checks.impact_signal: Traffic that cannot be attributed to a client
